reading.body:
UC Berkeley / vLLM Team's listed product is vLLM, categorized under open source & self-hosted models, with high-throughput inference engine as the function this data names first.

The data also tags vLLM with open-source and no external data sharing, description of what the product does rather than how well it does it. It also notes self-hosted, one of the few entries in this set where the product touches compute or physical infrastructure directly rather than sitting purely at the application layer.

Beyond the category, the product name, and this short list of tags tied to github.com, the data carries no user counts, revenue, funding, or headcount, so nothing here supports a claim about UC Berkeley / vLLM Team's scale or trajectory.

profile_text.body:
UC Berkeley / vLLM Team is recorded as a university lab and a non-profit organization. Its listed website is github.com. The text harvested from that site is GitHub's own description of itself: GitHub calls itself the world's most widely adopted AI-powered developer platform, where millions of developers, businesses, and the largest open source community build software, and it says it provides AI and automation tools for building and shipping software faster. That text describes GitHub, not the vLLM team.

The one product associated with the team is vLLM, described as a high-throughput inference engine that is open source and self-hosted, with no external data sharing. Its listed URL is the vllm-project/vllm repository on GitHub. No lawsuits, no MCP servers, and no SEC or patent facts are recorded for this organization.
